overall: AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: ballot, by-law, and authority allegations were declined as outside its jurisdiction, and the June 21 'Dispatch update' notice was held sufficient, though the AG recommended more descriptive topics.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly acted outside its authority by placing an advisory question on the election ballot instead of the Town Meeting warrant.
Complainant alleged the ballot question was confusing and that the ballot process was flawed.
allegations.key_passage: We also decline to review all allegations pertaining to the ballot process as well as allegations pertaining to the Board’s compliance with local by-laws and practices.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board disregarded the majority ballot vote against joining the Regional 9-1-1 Center when it later voted to join.
Complainant alleged the Board acted contrary to local by-laws or prior representations and practice in handling the 9-1-1 question.
allegations.key_passage: We also decline to review all allegations pertaining to the ballot process as well as allegations pertaining to the Board’s compliance with local by-laws and practices.

allegations.summary: June 21 notice listed only 'Dispatch update' though the Board voted to join the Regional 9-1-1 Center, so the public could not anticipate a vote or debate it.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board was not required to specify on the notice for the June 21 meeting that it would vote whether to join the Regional 9-1-1 Center, and the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not specifying in advance that a vote would be taken.

allegations.summary: AG raised on its own whether the topic 'Dispatch update' was sufficiently specific to advise the public of the anticipated discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We note concern that the topic “Dispatch update,” without more, may not have been sufficiently specific to reasonably advise the public that the anticipated discussion pertained to joining the Regional 9-1-1 Center.
